apps/server/src/peer/RemoteDelegation.ts.why: #386: a remote delegate_task interrupted after its launch there (the parent's turn moved on) still records and follows its task: the launch, record and follow run as one uninterruptible step. A launch recorded with no task here is stopped there with a warning, as a failed record is. Tested in apps/server/src/fork/remoteDelegationAbortSafe.test.ts. Upstream PR pingdotgg/t3code#30249 (record before launch) rewrites this block, and its intent differs: after an interrupted, uncertain launch it stops the child there, while this seam keeps the child and follows it. Whoever brings #30249 in through fork-follow must choose on purpose between stopping and keeping (and expect a merge conflict on this block), then drop this seam or keep it. Also #386: lastReply reads a task's reply through fork/remoteReplyRead.ts, which decodes the answer again without the thread's details when the full read does not decode, so a linked environment on another version (thread details missing a field this version requires) still delivers the reply. Tested in apps/server/src/fork/remoteReplyRead.test.ts. Also #532: a remote delegate_task carries its parent's resolved MCP profile in delegatedFrom (fork/remoteMcpProfile.ts), worked out before the uninterruptible launch so a refusal or an interrupt sends nothing; a profile narrower than all goes only to an environment whose GET /api/fork/features (fork/forkFeatures.ts, answered only to its link token) says mcpProfileCarry, and only to an instance there whose driver applies one (Claude; #661 asks that environment's orchestrator_capabilities for the launch's instance). Tested in apps/server/src/fork/remoteMcpProfile.test.ts.

scripts/prepare-server-compile-cache.cjs.why: #514: the macOS x64 build warms the server compile cache by running the x64 engine under Rosetta. Upstream's 120 s limit for that step fits its 12-core Mac runner, but on the fork's 3-core GitHub runner it took 116 s once and ran over once, failing the release. The fork's lines wrap the hook's own spawnSync with scripts/fork-cache-timeout.cjs, which raises a shorter limit to 360 s only when the step runs under Rosetta (no other target; a longer upstream limit is kept), and shadow spawnSync with it in the try block, so upstream's call line is unchanged. Tested in scripts/fork-cache-timeout.test.ts. Drop this seam when the fork builds macOS x64 on a bigger runner or upstream's limit is 360 s or more.

//pending: Upstream files whose fork lines predate counting every upstream file, each with its ceiling: the most fork lines it may hold against upstream (counted from upstream, as fork-follow runs the check). To move into fork files or pin as seams; lower a ceiling when lines move out and take a file off when none are left. A pull request may change them but not grow them.
//forkFiles: Files upstream does not have that are not named as fork files (a fork, fork-*, forkName or FORK_* folder or file). A pull request's run, which has no upstream commit, takes them for the fork's own. dir/ is everything under it, ** any folders, * any characters but /, !path never. A pattern that matches an upstream file fails the check from upstream.
//lost: Seam and pending files that lost upstream lines, counted from upstream (as fork-follow runs the check): "lines", the upstream lines not kept in order and indentation; "gone", those whose text is gone. Held exactly, like a ceiling; an unlisted file counts 0. Lower a count when a line comes back, and keep each one small: a count is not a set of lines, so a line counted here may move unseen, and in a pending file a pull request can put back one gone upstream line and delete another with both counts unchanged.
